description:
Return the delta feed for the world named by your API-Key header: every
element created/updated (`op: "upsert"`, full body) or deleted (`op:
"delete"`) since `since_cursor`, in apply order, in pages of `limit`
(default 25, max 1000). Entries carry FULL element bodies — a default page
stays inside any client's token budget; measured worlds ran ~1.5-2k chars
PER ENTRY, so raise `limit` only if you truly need bigger pages, and prefer
paging with the cursor.

Omit `since_cursor` (or pass "") to start from the beginning of the feed —
for a big world that is a multi-page walk, not one response. Pass the
returned `cursor` back as `since_cursor` to get the next page (or, later,
only what changed since); treat the cursor as OPAQUE. `has_more` true means
page again with the new cursor. Requires a READ or WRITE API-Key. This
mirrors `GET /api/v2/changes`.

`after` is for stepping into a world without a kept cursor: an ISO 8601
date and time (e.g. "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z"; no offset is UTC), and only
what changed at or after it comes back (an upsert whose `updated_at`, or a
delete whose `deleted_at`, is at or after it), so "the last day" is one
call. It is a filter, not a position: the order, `cursor` and `has_more`
are as without it; to read the whole window, pass `cursor` back as
`since_cursor` with the same `after`. The cursor is still the exact form
(every change once, in order): keep it if you will come back.

A guest key gets only what it may see, and no deletes: when its view of
the world changes, its cursor stops working and this tool says to pull
again from the start (omit `since_cursor`); keep what you hold that the
new walk does not name.
Where the server has the hidden mark on, a contributor's cursor works the
same way, and every delete says why (`reason`: `deleted`, or `hidden` for
an element hidden from you: drop your copy). There the reset says why too:
"reason role" (your role or membership changed: keep what the new walk
does not name) or "reason view" (what you may see changed: drop it), and
each page carries `epoch_reason` beside `epoch`. Never empty a copy on
your own.

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world): a key reads its own world only. list_worlds names the worlds you can read here.

name: get_changes
